correctness.rationale: The disjoint-shadow condition forces \(a+2b\le n-1\) using distinct weight-one descendants. Consecutively indexed adjacent-one words share a weight-two descendant, hence \(a\le\lceil(n-1)/2\rceil\). This proves the upper bound. The proposed two pair families achieve it, with their weight-one and weight-two descendants explicitly partitioned by parity and pair gap, respectively. Endpoints \(n=2\) onward are included. Finite checker independently recomputes shadows up to \(n=120\) and exact optima through \(n=12\).

value.rationale: Exact all-length capacity is a natural invariant for the sparse constant-weight-two subchannel of single-deletion correction. Weight partitioning is a documented coding method; knowing the maximum independent-set number, unlike chromatic bounds alone, settles the sharp weight-two rate and supplies simple explicit optimum designs. The result is not a mere finite table.
